title: Atoms and Molecules
seo_title: Grade 7 Atoms and Molecules Worksheets: Elements, Compounds and Chemical Formulas
standard_text: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on atoms and molecules (NGSS MS-PS1-1): elements and compounds, reading chemical formulas, subscripts and coefficients, molecule models and extended structures. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: A formula like H₂O shows the atoms in a molecule. Subscripts count atoms; coefficients count molecules.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of atoms. An element has only one kind of atom. Atoms join to form molecules; a compound has two or more kinds of atoms.

A chemical formula shows the atoms: in H2O, the subscript 2 means 2 hydrogen atoms, and O with no number means 1 oxygen atom. A coefficient in front counts molecules: 3H2O has 6 H and 3 O.

Some substances, like salt (NaCl) and diamond, form extended structures: huge repeating patterns of atoms instead of small molecules.

Example

How many atoms are in C6H12O6?

6 + 12 + 6

Answer: 24

Example

How many oxygen atoms are in 2CO2?

Each CO₂ has 2 O.

2 × 2

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

  • Reading H₂O as 2 oxygen atoms. The 2 belongs to H.
  • Thinking a subscript multiplies the whole formula. Only a coefficient does that.
  • Thinking O₂ is a compound. It has only one kind of atom, so it is an element.

faq.a: One molecule of water has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom.

faq.q: What is the difference between an element and a compound?
faq.a: An element has only one kind of atom. A compound has two or more kinds of atoms bonded together.

faq.q: What is the difference between a subscript and a coefficient?
faq.a: A subscript (small number after an element) counts atoms of that element. A coefficient (number in front) counts whole molecules.

items.q: How is a compound different from an element?
c: An element always has more atoms.
A compound has only one kind of atom.
A compound has two or more kinds of atoms bonded together; an element has only one kind.
items.e: Water is a compound; oxygen gas is an element.

items.q: Why do water and hydrogen peroxide have different properties even though both have H and O?
c: Properties do not depend on atoms.
They have different numbers and arrangements of atoms.
items.e: H₂O and H₂O₂ are different molecules.

items.q: What is a molecule?
c: two or more atoms joined together
